study_name.notes: No canonical study name/acronym given in the text.

subject_id.notes: No individual subject identifiers reported in the main text; may exist in Table S1 (not provided).

pmid.notes: PMID not stated within the provided paper text; paper_id supplied externally, not extracted from text.

subcohort.value: Central Africa and Indian peninsula travel groups
subcohort.evidence_quote: Seventeen traveled to Central Africa and 18 to the Indian peninsula
subcohort.notes: Two travel-destination subcohorts within the 35-subject study.

target_condition.evidence_quote: we used explorative shotgun metagenomic sequencing to address the abundance of >300 antibiotic resistance genes in fecal specimens
target_condition.notes: Study is not disease-focused; primary phenotype investigated is acquisition/increase of antibiotic resistance genes and microbiome composition change associated with international travel.

control.evidence_quote: fecal specimens from 35 Swedish students taken before and after exchange programs
control.notes: This is a paired before/after travel design, not a case-control study; no explicit case/control labeling given.

country.evidence_quote: Swedish students from the universities in Umeå, Stockholm, and Gothenburg traveling for international exchange studies
country.notes: Both before- and after-travel fecal specimens were collected in Sweden (before departure and after return to Sweden); travel destinations were the Indian peninsula and Central Africa but not the residence country.

body_site.evidence_quote: fecal specimens from 35 Swedish students taken before and after exchange programs

days_from_first_collection.evidence_quote: The fecal specimens were collected at a median of 4 days before departure (range 0 to 23) and 22 days (range 2 to 120) after return to Sweden.
days_from_first_collection.notes: Reported as separate medians for pre-departure and post-return sampling relative to travel, not as a single days-from-baseline value per sample.

lifestyle.notes: Not applicable; participants are Swedish university students, not a traditional/non-westernized population.

location.value: Umeå, Stockholm, Gothenburg (Sweden); travel destinations: Indian peninsula, Central Africa
location.evidence_quote: Swedish students from the universities in Umeå, Stockholm, and Gothenburg traveling for international exchange studies

westernized.evidence_quote: Swedish students from the universities in Umeå, Stockholm, and Gothenburg
westernized.notes: Inferred from participants being Swedish university students; term 'westernized' not used in the text.

antibiotics_exclusion_period.evidence_quote: None of the subjects included were allowed to have taken antibiotics within 6 months prior to fecal sampling.

antibiotics_exclusion_period_unit.evidence_quote: None of the subjects included were allowed to have taken antibiotics within 6 months prior to fecal sampling.

dna_extraction_kit.evidence_quote: DNA was extracted from the fecal specimens and sequenced using Illumina HiSeq 2000 technology.
dna_extraction_kit.notes: Extraction kit/protocol name not specified in main text; may be detailed in supplemental methods (not provided).

ncbi_accession.evidence_quote: Sequence data have been submitted to the European Nucleotide Archive under accession number PRJEB7369.

sequencing_platform.evidence_quote: DNA was extracted from the fecal specimens and sequenced using Illumina HiSeq 2000 technology.
sequencing_platform.notes: ESBL isolate genomes were separately sequenced with Illumina MiSeq (250-bp paired-end reads); metagenomic fecal samples used HiSeq 2000.

age.evidence_quote: Subjects were 23 to 34 years old, with a gender distribution of 74% females (26/35).
age.notes: Reported as a range for the whole cohort, not a single mean/median value; cannot be reduced to one number without fabrication.

age_group.notes: Derived from reported age range (23-34 years), which falls entirely within Adult category (18-65 years).

ancestry.notes: Ancestry not explicitly reported; only nationality (Swedish) given.

family.notes: Not applicable; no family-based sampling described.

family_role.notes: Not applicable; no family-based sampling described.

sex.evidence_quote: with a gender distribution of 74% females (26/35)
sex.notes: Reported as an aggregate cohort percentage (74% female, 26/35), not assignable as a single enum value at study level; would require sample-level data to assign per-subject sex.

zigosity.notes: Not a twin study; field not applicable.

age_min.notes: Age range reported for entire cohort of 35 subjects; not stratified by destination.

age_years.notes: Only an age range (23-34) is reported for the group, not individual ages.

antibiotics_current_use.evidence_quote: None of the subjects included were allowed to have taken antibiotics within 6 months prior to fecal sampling.
antibiotics_current_use.section: Materials and Methods — Subject selection and specimen collection
antibiotics_current_use.notes: Inferred 'No' current antibiotic use from the 6-month antibiotic exclusion criterion; not explicitly phrased as 'current use'.

disease.notes: No disease/condition mentioned for the study subjects (Swedish health-care students); inferred as healthy per field guidance, but not explicitly stated in text.

feces_phenotype.notes: Fecal specimens were collected but no specific stool phenotype (e.g., Bristol scale) reported.

treatment.evidence_quote: All travelers to Central Africa and 44% (8/18) of travelers to the Indian peninsula used antimalarial chemoprophylaxis.
treatment.notes: 100% (17/17) of Central Africa travelers and 44% (8/18) of Indian peninsula travelers used antimalarial chemoprophylaxis (e.g., mefloquine, proguanil, atovaquone mentioned in Discussion).

biomarker_name.evidence_quote: 2.6-fold increase for sulfonamide, 7.7-fold increase for trimethoprim, and 2.6-fold increase for beta-lactams
biomarker_name.section: Results — Abundance of resistance genes in the gut metagenome
biomarker_name.notes: These represent the three most prominent significant fold-change increases in resistance gene categories reported in the paper.

biomarker_unit.evidence_quote: 2.6-fold increase for sulfonamide, 7.7-fold increase for trimethoprim, and 2.6-fold increase for beta-lactams

biomarker_value.evidence_quote: 2.6-fold increase for sulfonamide, 7.7-fold increase for trimethoprim, and 2.6-fold increase for beta-lactams
biomarker_value.section: Results — Abundance of resistance genes in the gut metagenome
biomarker_value.notes: Corresponds in order to biomarker_name list: sulfonamide, trimethoprim, beta-lactams.

disease_response_os.notes: Study is a microbiome/antibiotic resistance investigation; overall survival not applicable.

ecog_performance_status.notes: Not applicable; study population is healthy students, not oncology patients.

feces_phenotype_value.notes: Fecal specimens were analyzed for taxonomic composition and resistance gene abundance, but no discrete 'feces_phenotype' variable with associated values was reported.

tumor_size_measurement.notes: Not applicable; no tumor-related data in this study.

tumor_size_residual_measurement.notes: Not applicable; no tumor-related data in this study.

value: 35 Swedish health care students (medical, nursing, dentistry) traveled to Indian peninsula (n=18) or Central Africa (n=17)
12/18 (67%) travelers to Indian peninsula acquired ESBL-producing E. coli after travel; none from Central Africa
All acquired ESBL-producing E. coli isolates carried CTX-M-15 gene
69% of subjects (12/17 Central Africa, 12/18 India) had travelers' diarrhea
Proteobacteria abundance increased after travel in 25/35 students
Study approved by regional ethical review board in Umeå, Sweden (2011-357-32M)
uncurated_metadata.evidence_quote: Of 18 students visiting the Indian peninsula, 12 acquired ESBL-producing Escherichia coli, while none returning from Africa were positive.
uncurated_metadata.notes: Supplementary contextual metadata not captured by other schema fields.

extraction_warnings: This paper reports cohort-level aggregate statistics (n=35 total, 17 Central Africa, 18 Indian peninsula) rather than per-subject/per-sample data; most schema fields intended for sample-level curation (subject_id, sample_id, individual age, individual sex, dna_extraction_kit, etc.) are not resolvable from the main text and are marked not_reported.
Detailed per-subject demographic and clinical data are referenced as being in Table S1/S2/S3/S4 in the supplemental material, which was not provided in the input text.

Age is reported only as a range (23-34 years) for the whole cohort; sex is reported only as an aggregate percentage (74% female); these cannot be assigned as single per-sample enum/number values without fabrication.

Two sequencing platforms were used for different purposes (Illumina HiSeq 2000 for metagenomic shotgun sequencing of fecal specimens; Illumina MiSeq for ESBL isolate genome sequencing); the schema field sequencing_platform was populated with the primary metagenomic platform (HiSeq).
Batch 1 returned granularity='subgroup_level', differs from batch 0 ('study_level'); kept batch 0.
Batch 1 subgroups ['Central Africa', 'Indian peninsula'] differ from batch 0 []; kept batch 0.

This paper is a metagenomics/microbiome travel study (not a cancer, twin, FMT, or neonatal study), so most schema fields (zygosity, BMI, HLA, tumor staging, obstetric/neonatal fields, disease response) are not applicable and were marked not_reported.
The 'disease' field value 'Healthy' was inferred (not explicitly stated in text) based on absence of any reported disease/condition in this cohort of exchange students; confidence set low.

Granularity was set to subgroup_level because destination-specific (Central Africa vs Indian peninsula) breakdowns exist for some variables (e.g., antimalarial prophylaxis use, ESBL acquisition), although several core demographic fields (age range, antibiotic use) were reported only at the whole-cohort level.

Antibiotics_current_use was derived from an antibiotic-exclusion criterion (no antibiotics within 6 months prior to sampling) rather than a direct statement about current use at time of study participation.

This paper is a microbiome/antibiotic resistance gene metagenomics study, not a clinical oncology or disease-response study; fields such as disease_response_os, ecog_performance_status, tumor_size_measurement, and tumor_size_residual_measurement are not applicable and were marked not_reported.

biomarker fields were interpreted as antibiotic resistance gene category fold-changes (sulfonamide, trimethoprim, beta-lactams), which is a non-standard use of 'biomarker' but represents the most quantifiable measurable indicators reported in the study.
feces_phenotype_value field description is ambiguous in this context; no explicit 'feces_phenotype' variable was defined in the paper, so it was marked not_reported.
